We start by writing the square root as a rational power,

$$
\sqrt x= x^{1/2}
$$

So, we can apply the power rule with

$$
n=\dfrac{1}{2}
$$

and get

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int\sqrt{x}dx &= \intx^{1/2}dx \\
&= (x^{1/2 + 1})/((\frac{1}{2} + 1)) + C \\
&= (x^{3/2})/((\frac{3}{2})) + C \\
&= \frac{2x^{3/2}}{3} + C
\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d}{dx}(\frac{2x^{3/2}}{3} + C) &=  \\
\frac{d}{dx}(\frac{2x^{3/2}}{3}) + \frac{d}{dx}(C) &=  \\
\frac{2}{3}\frac{d}{dx}(x^{3/2}) + 0 &=  \\
\frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{3}{2}x^{3/2 - 1} &=  \\
&= x^{1/2}✓
\end{aligned}
$$

We can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{1}{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{1/4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{1/4+1}}{(\frac{1}{4}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5/4}}{(\frac{5}{4})}+C \\  & =\frac{4{x}^{5/4}}{5}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{4{x}^{5/4}}{5}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{4{x}^{5/4}}{5})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{4}{5}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{5/4})+0 & = \\ \frac{4}{5}\cdot \frac{5}{4}{x}^{5/4-1} & = \\ {x}^{1/4}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the root as a rational power, $\sqrt[5]{{x}^{3}}={x}^{3/5}.$ So, we can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{3}{5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \sqrt[5]{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{3/5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3/5+1}}{(\frac{3}{5}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{8/5}}{(\frac{8}{5})}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{8/5}}{8}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{8/5}}{8}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{8/5}}{8})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{5}{8}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{8/5})+0 & = \\ \frac{5}{8}\cdot \frac{8}{5}{x}^{8/5-1} & = \\ {x}^{3/5}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the root as a rational power, $\sqrt[5]{{x}^{2}}={x}^{2/5}.$ So, we can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{2}{5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \sqrt[5]{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{2/5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2/5+1}}{(\frac{2}{5}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{7/5}}{(\frac{7}{5})}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{7/5}}{7}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{7/5}}{7}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{7/5}}{7})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{5}{7}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{7/5})+0 & = \\ \frac{5}{7}\cdot \frac{7}{5}{x}^{7/5-1} & = \\ {x}^{2/5}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\sqrt[3]{x}={x}^{1/3}$, we can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{1}{3}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{1/3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{1/3+1}}{(\frac{1}{3}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4/3}}{(\frac{4}{3})}+C \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{4/3}}{4}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's check our answer by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3{x}^{4/3}}{4}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3{x}^{4/3}}{4})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{3}{4}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4/3})+0 & = \\ \frac{3}{4}\cdot \frac{4}{3}{x}^{4/3-1} & = \\ {x}^{1/3}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

We can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{5}{2}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{5/2}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{5/2+1}}{(\frac{5}{2}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{7/2}}{(\frac{7}{2})}+C \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{7/2}}{7}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2{x}^{7/2}}{7}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2{x}^{7/2}}{7})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{2}{7}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{7/2})+0 & = \\ \frac{2}{7}\cdot \frac{7}{2}{x}^{7/2-1} & = \\ {x}^{5/2}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\sqrt[5]{x}={x}^{1/5}$, we can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{1}{5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{1/5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{1/5+1}}{(\frac{1}{5}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{6/5}}{(\frac{6}{5})}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{6/5}}{6}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's check our answer by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{6/5}}{6}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{6/5}}{6})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{5}{6}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{6/5})+0 & = \\ \frac{5}{6}\cdot \frac{6}{5}{x}^{6/5-1} & = \\ {x}^{1/5}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
